name: Risk (classic)

source.title: Risk rules (2010) copy hosted by Wizards of the Coast

setup.text: Give each player an army colour and keep the rest of each army as an off-board troop pile.
Leave the Cease Fire card out of the deck. It is not used in the classic game.
Roll a die to decide who goes first. Play runs clockwise.
Each player counts out a starting pool of troops.

by_count.2: No starting pool: your troops come from the dealt cards.

setup.text: In turn order, each player puts one troop from their pool on an empty territory to claim it. Repeat until all 42 territories are claimed.
Keep going in turn order, adding one troop at a time from your pool to territories you already hold, until every pool is empty. Then the first player takes the first turn.
Each player picks a colour. The three remaining colours are neutral armies.
Remove the Cease Fire card, shuffle the territory cards, then deal 12 to each player and 6 to each neutral army.
Place 1 troop on each territory shown by a 1-star card and 2 troops on each shown by a 2-star card, in the owner's colour. Do this for the neutral armies too.
Shuffle all the cards together into one deck. Set one troop of each neutral army to the side and tuck three face-down cards under each without looking.
Roll to see who goes first.

turn.summary: Your turn has four parts in order: place troops, attack, manoeuvre, then draw a card if you conquered something.
steps: Take 3 troops, plus bonus troops for territories held (12-14 territories +1, 15-17 +2, and so on up to +10 for 40-42), for any whole continent held, and for cards you hand in. Place all of them on territories you control.

Attack as many times as you like, or not at all. Pick one of your territories, and an enemy territory joined to it by a border or sea line. Attack with 1 to 3 troops, always leaving at least 1 behind.

Attacker rolls one black die per attacking troop; defender rolls one red die per defending troop, using 1 or 2 troops. Pair dice from highest to lowest. A higher attack die removes a defender; equal or higher defence removes an attacker.
If the defending territory is emptied, move in your surviving attackers, plus as many more as you wish from the attacking territory, keeping 1 behind.
Manoeuvre once at the end: move any number of troops from one of your territories to another that is linked to it through a chain of your own territories.
If you conquered at least one territory this turn, draw one card. Never draw more than one per turn.

end: In the classic game, a player wins by controlling all 42 territories, which means every opponent is eliminated. In the two-player game you also win by holding 30 territories at the end of your turn.

scoring.text: There are no points. The winner is the last player standing with every territory.

missed.text: The defender wins ties on each pair of dice.
Unpaired extra dice are ignored. The lowest dice are the ones dropped.
You must leave at least 1 troop in the territory you attack from. The defender may use their last troop to fight.
You can only draw one card per turn, however many territories you took.
If you wipe out a player's last territory, you take all of their cards.
In a two-player game you may add 3 troops to one neutral army at the start of your turn, spread across its territories. Only one neutral army per turn.
In a two-player game, conquering a neutral army's last territory gives you the 3 cards that were hidden under its troop.

not_covered: Introductory Game (shorter variant with the Cease Fire card, territory targets and dealt starting territories).
Exact bonus troops for cards handed in, for each continent, and when a hand-in is compulsory: the chart and continent values are printed on the board, not in the rulebook text.
unverified: Troops-for-cards chart and per-continent bonus values (printed on the board). The territory bonus bands (12-14 = +1 up to 40-42 = +10) are in the text.
